title: Princeton advisory council and the National Endowment for the Arts
summary: Carter accepted seats on Princeton's music advisory council and the NEA council reviewing applications.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Well, that brings us down, really, very close to the present, and your -- I just want to follow up with, and get on to the record, a couple more academic assignments or appointments which have followed since this perhaps, this new episode, we might call it, or set of events, beginning in the late sixties.
I think that you had an invitation from the Princeton music department, recently.
Yes That was to join the Advisory Council of the music department, and I was very pleased with the invitation. I accepted, and I am now a member of the Advisory Council.
And then you had another one from Washington?
Yes, that was from the National Endowment Fund.
You mean the National Endowment for the Arts.
Yes, the National Endowment for the Arts -- and I accepted that also.
That's an advisory council position, too, in a manner of speaking.
I think it is, yes. Yes, it is.
You have just attended a meeting of that Council.
Yes, the first set of meetings.
What was the task of the group of which you were a member?

Well, it was looking over the applications and picking out those that, you know, would recommend -- evaluating, I should say, you know. And primarily that's what we were involved in this last set of meetings, and also -- we're gonna be working on the guidelines.
